name: General Trivia
description: Fascinating curiosities, arts, literature, and worldwide facts across 11 levels.

questions.question: Which sea creature is famous for having three hearts and blue blood?
questions.explanation: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, while one pumps oxygenated blood through the body.

questions.question: What is the only mammal capable of sustained true powered flight?
questions.explanation: Bats are the only mammals whose forelimbs form webbed wings capable of true flapping flight.

questions.question: What is the tallest living mammal on Earth?
questions.explanation: Adult giraffes can stand between 14 to 19 feet (4.3 to 5.8 meters) tall.

questions.question: What natural food item produced by insects is known to never truly spoil if sealed?
questions.explanation: Archaeologists have found pots of 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that remains perfectly edible.

questions.question: Which animal is recognized as the slowest-moving mammal in the world?
questions.explanation: Three-toed sloths move at an average speed of about 0.15 mph (0.24 km/h) through tree canopies.

questions.question: What color is a polar bear's skin beneath its thick white fur?
questions.explanation: A polar bear's skin is black to absorb heat from sunlight, while its fur is translucent and hollow.

questions.question: What is a group of flamingos appropriately called?
questions.explanation: A gathering of flamingos is known as a flamboyance, matching their vibrant pink plumage.

questions.question: Which continent is the natural native habitat of the wild platypus and koala?
questions.explanation: Both the duck-billed platypus and koala are endemic to the Australian continent.

questions.question: How many arms (tentacles and arms combined) does a typical squid have?
questions.explanation: Squids have eight arms and two longer feeding tentacles, totaling ten appendages.

questions.question: What is the largest living species of bird in the world, unable to fly?
questions.explanation: The common ostrich can weigh up to 300 pounds and sprint at speeds up to 43 mph (70 km/h).

questions.question: Who painted the world-renowned portrait of the Mona Lisa in the 16th century?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci began painting the Mona Lisa (La Gioconda) in Florence around 1503.

questions.question: Which Dutch post-impressionist painter created 'The Starry Night' while staying in Saint-Rémy?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night in June 1889 depicting the view from his asylum room window.

questions.question: Who sculpted the famous 17-foot marble statue of David in Florence?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo Buonarroti sculpted David out of a single block of Carrara marble between 1501 and 1504.

questions.question: Which Norwegian artist created the iconic expressionist painting 'The Scream'?
questions.explanation: Edvard Munch created four versions of The Scream between 1893 and 1910.

questions.question: Who painted the famous ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican between 1508 and 1512?
questions.explanation: Pope Julius II commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling depicting scenes from Genesis.

questions.question: Which Spanish artist co-founded Cubism and painted the anti-war masterpiece 'Guernica' in 1937?
questions.explanation: Picasso created Guernica in response to the bombing of the Basque town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War.

questions.question: Who painted 'The Persistence of Memory' featuring melting pocket watches in a desolate landscape?
questions.explanation: Salvador Dalí painted the surrealist classic in 1931, inspired by soft Camembert cheese melting in the sun.

questions.question: Which Dutch artist painted 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' around 1665?
questions.explanation: Johannes Vermeer is renowned for his mastery of light in masterworks like Girl with a Pearl Earring.

questions.question: Who sculpted the famous bronze statue 'The Thinker' (Le Penseur)?
questions.explanation: Rodin originally conceived The Thinker in 1880 as part of his monumental portal 'The Gates of Hell'.

questions.question: Which Mexican painter is internationally celebrated for her uncompromising and vibrant self-portraits?
questions.explanation: Frida Kahlo's folk-art influenced work explored identity, suffering, and Mexican culture.

questions.question: Who wrote the tragic play 'Romeo and Juliet' and the tragedy 'Hamlet'?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare produced roughly 39 plays and 154 sonnets during the Elizabethan and Jacobean eras.

questions.question: Who wrote the dystopian novel 'Nineteen Eighty-Four' featuring Big Brother and Thoughtcrime?
questions.explanation: Eric Arthur Blair, writing under the pen name George Orwell, published Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949.

questions.question: Which Spanish author wrote 'Don Quixote', widely considered the first modern European novel?
questions.explanation: Cervantes published Don Quixote in two parts (1605 and 1615), satirizing chivalric romances.

questions.question: Who wrote the epic fantasy trilogy 'The Lord of the Rings'?
questions.explanation: Oxford philology professor J.R.R. Tolkien created Middle-earth, publishing the trilogy between 1954 and 1955.

questions.question: Who authored the classic 1813 novel 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explanation: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice anonymously in 1813, following Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy.

questions.question: Who wrote the iconic 1818 gothic horror novel 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus'?
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein at age 18 during a rainy summer at Lake Geneva in 1816.

questions.question: Which Russian author wrote the sweeping historical epic novel 'War and Peace'?
questions.explanation: Count Leo Tolstoy published War and Peace in 1869, chronicling the French invasion of Russia.

questions.question: Who created the legendary fictional detective Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John Watson?
questions.explanation: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Sherlock Holmes in the 1887 novel 'A Study in Scarlet'.

questions.question: Who wrote the famous children's fantasy novel 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' in 1865?
questions.explanation: Oxford mathematician Charles Lutwidge Dodgson wrote Alice under the pseudonym Lewis Carroll.

questions.question: Which French novelist wrote 'Les Misérables' and 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame'?
questions.explanation: Victor Hugo was a titan of the French Romantic movement and passionate advocate for social justice.

questions.question: In which Italian city did the traditional Neapolitan pizza and Pizza Margherita originate?
questions.explanation: Naples is the birthplace of modern pizza; pizzaiolo Raffaele Esposito created the Margherita in 1889.

questions.question: In which country was the beverage of tea first discovered and cultivated thousands of years ago?
questions.explanation: According to legend, Chinese Emperor Shennong discovered tea when camellia leaves blew into boiling water in 2737 BCE.

questions.question: What spice, derived from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower, is the world's most expensive spice by weight?
questions.explanation: Saffron requires harvesting up to 75,000 crocus sativus blossoms by hand to produce a single pound.

questions.question: Which ancient Mesoamerican civilization first brewed bitter chocolate drinks from cacao beans?
questions.explanation: The Maya and Aztecs prepared frothy ceremonial cacao beverages called 'xocolatl'.

questions.question: What pastry, famous in French cuisine, actually originated in Vienna, Austria, as the 'Kipferl'?
questions.explanation: The croissant evolved from the Austrian crescent-shaped yeast bread Kipferl, introduced to Paris in the 1830s.

questions.question: What Japanese dish traditionally consists of vinegared rice served with seafood, vegetables, or egg?
questions.explanation: The word 'sushi' refers specifically to the seasoned sumeshi rice, not raw fish.

questions.question: Which country is historically credited with the discovery and early cultivation of the coffee plant?
questions.explanation: Legend attributes the discovery of coffee to an Ethiopian goat herder named Kaldi in the Kaffa province.

questions.question: What French cooking technique involves vacuum-sealing food in a bag and cooking it in a precise water bath?
questions.explanation: Sous-vide (French for 'under vacuum') enables exact temperature control and moisture retention.

questions.question: What cheese with a blue-veined mold originates from raw sheep's milk aged in natural caves in southern France?
questions.explanation: Roquefort is aged in the natural Combalou limestone caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

questions.question: What essential cooking fat is produced by extracting oil from the fruit of the Olea europaea tree?
questions.explanation: Olive oil has been a staple of Mediterranean agriculture and cuisine for over 6,000 years.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The Japanese yen (JPY) was adopted under the Meiji government in 1871.

questions.question: What is the official currency of the United Kingdom, recognized as the oldest continuously used currency?
questions.explanation: The British Pound Sterling has been in continuous circulation for over 1,200 years since Anglo-Saxon times.

questions.question: What is the currency used by Switzerland and Liechtenstein?
questions.explanation: The Swiss Franc (CHF) is noted for its stability and international reserve status.

questions.question: What international financial center on Manhattan island in New York City is famous as the hub of American finance?
questions.explanation: Wall Street houses the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and major financial institutions.

questions.question: What precious yellow metal has served as a universal store of value and currency basis throughout history?
questions.explanation: Gold has been minted into coins and held in central bank reserves for millennia due to its rarity and corrosion resistance.

questions.question: What is the official national currency of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian Rupee (INR) is issued and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.question: What is the term for a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services over time?
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money over time as prices rise.

questions.question: What international organization based in Washington, D.C. works to foster global monetary cooperation and financial stability?
questions.explanation: The IMF was established at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 to support global financial stability.

questions.question: What term in finance describes a market condition where prices are consistently rising and investor optimism is high?
questions.explanation: A bull market is characterized by rising stock valuations, contrasting with a bear market.

questions.question: What is the official currency of South Korea?
questions.explanation: The South Korean Won (KRW) has been the currency of the Republic of Korea since 1962.

questions.question: What was the first full-length cel-animated feature film produced by Walt Disney in 1937?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.explanation: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was a massive critical and commercial milestone in cinematic history.

questions.question: Which legendary English rock band from Liverpool consisted of John, Paul, George, and Ringo?
questions.explanation: The Beatles are the best-selling music act of all time, with estimated sales over 600 million units.

questions.question: What award statuette presented annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is nicknamed?
questions.explanation: The Academy Award statuette of a knight holding a crusader's sword is affectionately known as the Oscar.

questions.question: Which Michael Jackson album released in November 1982 became the best-selling album of all time?
questions.explanation: Thriller has sold an estimated 70 million copies worldwide and won eight Grammy Awards in 1984.

questions.question: Who directed the classic Hollywood cinema masterworks 'Jaws', 'E.T.', 'Jurassic Park', and 'Schindler's List'?
questions.explanation: Steven Spielberg is the highest-grossing film director in history.

questions.question: What sci-fi film franchise created by George Lucas debuted with 'A New Hope' in May 1977?
questions.explanation: Star Wars revolutionized cinematic visual effects, merchandising, and modern blockbuster culture.

questions.question: Which classical Austrian composer was a child prodigy who composed over 600 works before dying at age 35?
questions.explanation: Mozart began composing at age 5 and produced masterwork operas, symphonies, and concertos.

questions.question: What 1997 James Cameron epic romance and disaster film won 11 Oscars and starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet?
questions.explanation: Titanic grossed over $2 billion and was the first film to reach that box office milestone.

questions.question: Which American singer-songwriter is known as 'The Queen of Pop' and the best-selling female recording artist of all time?
questions.explanation: Madonna has sold over 300 million records worldwide certified by Guinness World Records.

questions.question: What annual international song competition organized by the EBU has been broadcast live since 1956?
questions.explanation: Eurovision is one of the world's longest-running and most-watched non-sporting television events.

questions.question: Which language has the highest number of native (first-language) speakers in the world?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese has approximately 920 million native speakers, primarily in China.

questions.question: What is the official language of Brazil, contrasting with the Spanish spoken across most of South America?
questions.explanation: Portuguese is the official language due to Portuguese colonization beginning under Pedro Álvares Cabral in 1500.

questions.question: What ancient writing system used stylized pictorial characters to represent sounds and ideas in ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: Egyptian hieroglyphs were deciphered in 1822 by Jean-François Champollion using the Rosetta Stone.

questions.question: What international auxiliary language was created in 1887 by L.L. Zamenhof to facilitate universal communication?
questions.explanation: Esperanto is the most widely spoken constructed international language in the world.

questions.question: Which language family includes English, Spanish, Russian, Hindi, and Persian?
questions.explanation: Indo-European is the world's largest language family by number of speakers.

questions.question: Which ancient Semitic alphabet developed around 1050 BCE served as the ancestor to Greek, Latin, and Arabic scripts?
questions.explanation: The 22-letter Phoenician consonant alphabet was adopted and adapted across the Mediterranean.

questions.question: What is the study of language structure, sounds, grammar, and evolution called?
questions.explanation: Linguistics encompasses phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics.

questions.question: Which language is the official sacred liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism?
questions.explanation: Sanskrit is an ancient Indo-Aryan language in which the Vedas and Upanishads were composed.

questions.question: What term describes a word that is spelled identically backwards and forwards (like 'radar' or 'racecar')?
questions.explanation: A palindrome reads the same backwards and forwards, disregarding spaces and punctuation.

questions.question: Which modern Romance language is most closely related to ancient classical Latin?
questions.explanation: Italian and Sardinian retain the closest phonological and grammatical proximity to Latin.

questions.question: Who was the king of the gods and ruler of Mount Olympus in ancient Greek mythology?
questions.explanation: Zeus wielded the thunderbolt and governed the sky and heavens in Greek myth.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, who is the hammer-wielding god associated with lightning, thunder, and storms?
questions.explanation: Thor carries the magical crusher hammer Mjölnir to protect mankind and Asgard.

questions.question: Which ancient Egyptian jackal-headed god presided over mummification and the afterlife?
questions.explanation: Anubis guided souls to the underworld and weighed their hearts against the feather of Ma'at.

questions.question: In Roman mythology, who was the god of war, equivalent to the Greek god Ares?
questions.explanation: Mars was revered as a father figure and protector of the Roman people and legions.

questions.question: Who was the legendary British leader of the Knights of the Round Table at Camelot?
questions.explanation: Arthurian legends center on King Arthur, Merlin, Excalibur, and the quest for the Holy Grail.

questions.question: In Greek mythology, what hero completed Twelve Labors including slaying the Nemean Lion?
questions.explanation: Heracles completed twelve legendary tasks commanded by King Eurystheus to atone for a madness-induced tragedy.

questions.question: In Hindu mythology, which deity is worshipped as the remover of all obstacles, depicted with an elephant head?
questions.explanation: Lord Ganesha is patron of letters, learning, and new beginnings.

questions.question: What mythical bird is famous in folklore for bursting into flames and rising reborn from its own ashes?
questions.explanation: The phoenix is a universal symbol of renewal, immortality, and resurrection.

questions.question: What one-eyed giants forged thunderbolts for Zeus in Greek mythology?
questions.explanation: The Cyclopes were giant beings with a single circular eye in the center of their forehead.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, what is the great hall in Asgard where fallen warriors feast with Odin?
questions.explanation: Valkyries chose heroic dead warriors from battlefields and conducted them to Valhalla.

questions.question: Who invented the modern ballpoint pen in the 1930s, giving his name to the pen in many countries?
questions.explanation: Hungarian journalist László Bíró developed the rolling-ball quick-drying ink pen.

questions.question: What adhesive stationery item was accidentally invented by 3M scientist Spencer Silver in 1968?
questions.explanation: Dr. Silver created a low-tack reusable adhesive, later applied to paper bookmarks by Art Fry.

questions.question: What kitchen appliance was discovered accidentally by Percy Spencer in 1945 when a candy bar melted in his pocket near a radar magnetron?
questions.explanation: Percy Spencer at Raytheon noticed the radar tube melted his chocolate and built the first Radarrange.

questions.question: What hook-and-loop fastening fabric was invented by George de Mestral in 1941 after burrs stuck to his dog's fur?
questions.explanation: De Mestral examined cocklebur burs under a microscope and patented 'Velcro' (velours + crochet).

questions.question: Who invented the modern safety elevator equipped with a fall-prevention brake in 1852?
questions.explanation: Elisha Otis dramatically demonstrated his safety elevator brake at the 1854 New York World's Fair.

questions.question: Who patented the first commercially successful sewing machine mechanism in the US in 1846?
questions.explanation: Elias Howe patented the lockstitch sewing machine using an eye-pointed needle and shuttle.

questions.question: What safety glass laminated with a transparent plastic interlayer was invented accidentally by Édouard Bénédictus in 1903?
questions.explanation: Bénédictus dropped a glass flask coated with dried cellulose nitrate and observed it shattered without flying apart.

questions.question: Who invented dynamite in 1867 by stabilizing nitroglycerin with kieselguhr (diatomaceous earth)?
questions.explanation: Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel patented dynamite and later bequeathed his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes.

questions.question: What ubiquitous fastener was patented as the 'hookless fastener' by Gideon Sundbäck in 1914?
questions.explanation: Sundbäck perfected the interlocking metal teeth fastener, later dubbed the 'zipper' by B.F. Goodrich.

questions.question: Who invented vulcanized rubber in 1839 by heating natural rubber with sulfur?
questions.explanation: Goodyear's vulcanization process made rubber weatherproof, durable, and elastic.

questions.question: What distinct leaf symbol is prominently featured on the national flag of Canada?
questions.explanation: The stylized red eleven-pointed maple leaf has been Canada's official national flag emblem since 1965.

questions.question: How many stars and stripes are featured on the national flag of the United States?
questions.explanation: The 50 white stars represent the 50 states; the 13 alternating red and white stripes represent the original 13 colonies.

questions.question: What is unique about the national flag of Nepal compared to all other sovereign nations?
questions.explanation: Nepal has the world's only non-quadrilateral sovereign flag, formed by two overlapping triangular pennants.

questions.question: What three national flags are combined to form the British 'Union Jack'?
options: England, Scotland, and Northern Ireland (Saint George, Saint Andrew, Saint Patrick)
questions.explanation: The Union Flag merges the crosses of St. George (England), St. Andrew (Scotland), and St. Patrick (Ireland).

questions.question: What national flag features a golden wheel known as the 'Ashoka Chakra' in its center?
questions.explanation: The Indian tricolor (Tiranga) features the 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra in navy blue on a white middle stripe.

questions.question: What tree is centered on the national flag of Lebanon?
questions.explanation: The green cedar of Lebanon has symbolized resilience, peace, and eternity in the region since Biblical times.

questions.question: Which country's flag features an image of an AK-47 assault rifle along with a hoe and a book?
questions.explanation: Mozambique's flag incorporates an AK-47 with bayonet representing national defense and vigilance.

questions.question: How many stars are displayed on the flag of the European Union?
questions.explanation: The EU flag features a circle of 12 gold stars on a blue background, symbolizing unity and perfection (not the number of member states).

questions.question: What color are the five stars on the red flag of the People's Republic of China?
questions.explanation: The flag of China features one large golden star surrounded by four smaller golden stars in an arc.

questions.question: What national flag features an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus devouring a snake?
questions.explanation: The Mexican coat of arms depicts the ancient Aztec foundation prophecy of Tenochtitlan.

questions.question: Why are flamingos naturally pink?
options: Their diet is high in carotenoid pigments from shrimp and algae
questions.explanation: Flamingos are born with grey feathers; their pink coloration comes from digesting beta-carotene in brine shrimp and algae.

questions.question: Botanically speaking, which of the following is classified as a true berry?
questions.explanation: In botanical terms, bananas, tomatoes, and watermelons are berries, while strawberries and raspberries are aggregate fruits.

questions.question: Did Cleopatra VII live chronologically closer in time to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza or the Apollo 11 moon landing?
questions.explanation: The Pyramids were built ~2500 BCE; Cleopatra lived ~30 BCE (2470 years later); the Moon landing was in 1969 CE (2000 years after Cleopatra).

questions.question: Which historic university was founded earlier than the rise of the Aztec Empire in central Mexico?
questions.explanation: Teaching existed at Oxford as early as 1096 CE; the Aztec civilization was founded around 1325 CE.

questions.question: How many hearts does an earthworm have?
questions.explanation: Earthworms possess five pairs of aortic arches that function as five hearts pumping blood through vessels.

questions.question: What is the only letter in the English alphabet that does NOT appear in the name of any US state?
questions.explanation: The letter 'Q' does not appear in any of the 50 US state names.

questions.question: What animal has fingerprints so identical to humans that they have confused crime scene detectives?
questions.explanation: Koalas have dermatoglyph patterns on their finger pads nearly indistinguishable from human fingerprints.

questions.question: Which country has more pyramids than Egypt?
questions.explanation: Sudan has between 200 and 255 ancient pyramids built by the Kingdom of Kush, exceeding Egypt's ~118-138.

questions.question: What color was the original carrot before Dutch cultivators bred orange varieties in the 17th century?
questions.explanation: Early wild and cultivated carrots in Central Asia were predominantly purple or yellow.

questions.question: What is the total number of dots on a pair of standard six-sided dice?
questions.explanation: One die has 1+2+3+4+5+6 = 21 pips (dots), so a pair has exactly 42 pips.
